questions.knowledgeNote: An equation true for ALL values is an identity; one true for SOME values is a (conditional) equation.
questions.question: AQ1(a). What does the trigonometrical equation mean?
questions.solution: An equation involving trigonometric functions of an unknown angle (variable) is a trigonometrical equation. It is 'conditional': unlike an identity (true for every admissible value), it holds only for specific values - e.g. sin x = 1/2 is satisfied by x = 30deg but not by x = 45deg (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: Roots are the specific angles that satisfy the equation.
questions.question: AQ1(b). What is the solution (root) of a trigonometrical equation?
questions.solution: Any particular value of the unknown angle that satisfies the equation is a solution (root) - e.g. x = 30deg and x = 150deg are roots of sin x = 1/2, since both satisfy it (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: Periodicity makes roots infinite: the general solution packages them all with an integer n.
questions.question: AQ1(c). What is the general value (general solution) of a trigonometrical equation?
questions.solution: Because trig functions repeat every 360deg, an equation has infinitely many roots (e.g. sin x = 1/2 holds at 30deg, 150deg and every coterminal angle). The set of ALL solutions, written with an arbitrary integer n, is the general solution - e.g. x = n.360deg+30deg or n.360deg+150deg (book Section 4.2).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q1; book p155 = PDF p182; answer from Section 4.2 text

questions.knowledgeNote: sin2x+sin6x = 2sin4xcos2x: the whole row collapses on sin4x.
questions.question: AQ2(i). Solve sin2x + sin4x + sin6x = 0.
questions.solution: (sin2x+sin6x)+sin4x = 2sin4xcos2x+sin4x = sin4x(2cos2x+1) = 0. sin4x = 0: x = n.pi/4. cos2x = -1/2: x = n.pi +- pi/3. Verified: x = pi/4 gives 1+0-1 = 0; x = pi/3 gives 0. (Key's 'n.pi/4' fraction partially legible; both families verified.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (200-dpi image read); verified by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: Half the equation, then everything in cos2x: -cos2x(cos2x+1) = 0.
questions.question: AQ2(ii). Solve 2sin^2x + sin^2 2x = 2.
questions.solution: sin^2x(1+2cos^2x) = 1; with sin^2x = (1-cos2x)/2 and 2sin^2xcos^2x = sin^2 2x/2: 1-cos2x+sin^2 2x = 2 gives -cos2x(cos2x+1) = 0. cos2x = 0: x = n.pi+pi/2... i.e. odd multiples: x = (2n+1).pi/4? No: cos2x = 0 gives 2x = (2n+1).pi/2, x = (2n+1).pi/4 (odd pi/4s). cos2x = -1: x = (2n+1).pi/2. Union: x = (2n+1).pi/4 or (2n+1).pi/2 - equivalently n.pi+pi/2 or n.pi+-pi/4. Matches the key: 'n.pi+pi/2, n.pi+-pi/4'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); matches key

questions.question: AQ2(iii). Solve 2sin^2x + 3cosx = 0 (0 < x < 2pi).
questions.solution: 2cos^2x-3cosx-2 = (2cosx+1)(cosx-2) = 0. cosx = 2 impossible. cosx = -1/2: in (0, 2pi): x = 2pi/3, 4pi/3. Verified: x = 2pi/3 gives 2(3/4)+3(-1/2) = 0. (Key's '2pi/3, 4pi/3' fragments match.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(iii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); |cos|<=1 enforced

questions.question: AQ2(iv). Solve sin^2theta - costheta = 1/4 (0 <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: 1-cos^2-cos-1/4 = 0 gives cos^2+cos-3/4 = 0: costheta = 1/2 (other root -3/2 rejected). In [0, 2pi]: theta = pi/3, 5pi/3. Verified: sin^2(pi/3)-cos(pi/3) = 3/4-1/2 = 1/4.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); |cos|<=1 enforced

questions.question: Q2(v). Solve 2tantheta - cottheta = -1.
questions.solution: 2tan^2theta+tantheta-1 = (2tantheta-1)(tantheta+1) = 0 (tantheta != 0 throughout). tantheta = 1/2: theta = n.pi+alpha (alpha = tan^(-1)(1/2)). tantheta = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. Both verified. (Key's 'n.pi+alpha' fragment matches.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(v); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); tantheta != 0 respected

questions.question: AQ2(vi). Solve tan^2theta + (1-sqrt(3))tantheta - sqrt(3) = 0.
questions.solution: (tantheta+1)(tantheta-sqrt(3)) = 0. tantheta = -1: theta = n.pi-pi/4. tantheta = sqrt(3): theta = n.pi+pi/3. Verified: theta = pi/3 gives 3+(1-sqrt(3))sqrt(3)-sqrt(3) = 3+sqrt(3)-3-sqrt(3) = 0.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q2(vi); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); verified by substitution

questions.question: AQ3(i). Solve sintheta + costheta = 1/sqrt(2) (0 <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: sin(theta+pi/4) = 1/2: theta+pi/4 = pi/6, 5pi/6 (+2pi). In range: theta = 7pi/12 (from 5pi/6) and theta = 23pi/12 (from pi/6+2pi). theta = -pi/12 and 25pi/12 excluded. Verified: sin(7pi/12)+cos(7pi/12) = 0.707. (Key's '/12' fragments consistent.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.question: AQ3(ii). Solve costheta - sintheta = 1/sqrt(2) (-2pi <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: cos(theta+pi/4) = 1/2: theta = 2n.pi+pi/12 or 2n.pi-7pi/12. Inside [-2pi, 2pi]: -23pi/12, -7pi/12, pi/12, 17pi/12. Verified: theta = pi/12 gives 0.966-0.259 = 0.707.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: (sin+1)/cos = sqrt(3): 2sin(theta-pi/3) = -1 - and 3pi/2 must be thrown out (tan/sec undefined).
questions.question: AQ3(iii). Solve tantheta + sectheta = sqrt(3) [T.U. 2050].
questions.solution: sin+1 = sqrt(3)cos gives 2sin(theta-pi/3) = -1: sin(theta-pi/3) = -1/2, theta = 2n.pi+pi/6 or 2n.pi+3pi/2. theta = 3pi/2 (mod 2pi) makes tan/sec undefined - rejected. So theta = 2n.pi+pi/6. Verified: tan(pi/6)+sec(pi/6) = 1/sqrt(3)+2/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(iii) [T.U. 2050]; book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); undefined branch rejected

questions.question: AQ3(iv). Solve sqrt(2)sectheta + tantheta = 1.
questions.solution: sqrt(2)+sintheta = costheta gives sin(theta-pi/4)... sin -cos = -sqrt(2): sqrt(2)sin(theta-pi/4) = -sqrt(2), sin(theta-pi/4) = -1: theta = 2n.pi-pi/4 (cos != 0 throughout). Verified: sqrt(2)(sqrt(2))+(-1) = 1. (Key's '2n.pi-pi/4' fragment matches.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); matches key, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: 2sin(theta+pi/3) = 1: four hits in the open interval (-2pi, 2pi).
questions.question: AQ3(v). Solve sqrt(3)costheta + sintheta = 1 (-2pi < theta < 2pi) [T.U. 2052].
questions.solution: sin(theta+pi/3) = 1/2: theta = n.pi+(-1)^n.pi/6-pi/3. Inside (-2pi, 2pi): -7pi/6, -pi/6, pi/2, 11pi/6 (endpoints -2pi, 2pi excluded as strict). Verified: theta = pi/2 gives 0+1 = 1; theta = -pi/6 gives 3/2-1/2 = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(v) [T.U. 2052]; book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); interval filter applied, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Amplitude sqrt(1+3) = 2 equals the RHS: sin(...) = 1 is the ONLY way - two hits in [-2pi, 2pi].
questions.question: AQ3(vi). Solve costheta + sqrt(3)sintheta = 2 (-2pi <= theta <= 2pi).
questions.solution: 2sin(theta+pi/6) = 2: sin(theta+pi/6) = 1, theta = 2n.pi+pi/3. In [-2pi, 2pi]: theta = -5pi/3, pi/3. Verified: theta = pi/3 gives 1/2+3/2 = 2; theta = -5pi/3 gives 1/2+3/2 = 2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q3(vi); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); maximum-attainment argument, verified

questions.knowledgeNote: sin = 1/2 meets cos = -sqrt(3)/2 in QII: x = 2n.pi+5pi/6.
questions.question: AQ4(i). Find the general x with sinx = 1/2 and cosx = -sqrt(3)/2.
questions.solution: sinx = 1/2 at pi/6, 5pi/6 (+2pi); cosx = -sqrt(3)/2 at 5pi/6, 7pi/6 (+2pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/6 (second quadrant, as required). (Key's '2n.pi+5pi/6' fragments match.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(i); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection

questions.knowledgeNote: sin = -1/sqrt(2) meets tan = 1 in QIII: x = 2n.pi+5pi/4.
questions.question: AQ4(ii). Find the general x with sinx = -1/sqrt(2) and tanx = 1.
questions.solution: sinx = -1/sqrt(2) at 5pi/4, 7pi/4 (+2pi); tanx = 1 at pi/4, 5pi/4 (+pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/4 (third quadrant). Verified: sin(5pi/4) = -1/sqrt(2), tan(5pi/4) = 1.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(ii); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection

questions.knowledgeNote: The book prints the full quadrant argument for this one: QIV gives 2n.pi+5pi/3.
questions.question: AQ4(iii). Find the general x with sinx = -sqrt(3)/2 and cosx = 1/2 (hint printed in the book).
questions.solution: Sine negative + cosine positive: fourth quadrant. x = 2pi-pi/3 = 5pi/3 satisfies both; with 2pi periodicity: x = 2n.pi+5pi/3. (Reproduces the book's printed hint, book p155.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(iii); book p155 = PDF p182 (hint printed in book)

questions.knowledgeNote: cosec = -2/sqrt(3) gives sin = -sqrt(3)/2 (QIII/QIV); tan = -sqrt(3) keeps only QIV: 5pi/3.
questions.question: AQ4(iv). Find the general x with cosecx = -2/sqrt(3) and tanx = -sqrt(3).
questions.solution: sinx = -sqrt(3)/2 at 4pi/3, 5pi/3 (+2pi); tanx = -sqrt(3) at 2pi/3, 5pi/3 (+pi). Common: x = 2n.pi+5pi/3 (fourth quadrant). Verified: cosec(5pi/3) = -2/sqrt(3), tan(5pi/3) = -sqrt(3).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.4 Additional Q4(iv); book p155 = PDF p182 (image read); quadrant intersection
